Amazing trail, really great views. Loved that it was spacious and clean as well!

Cemetery is a very nice walk.
It is a great trail with a mix of elevation, featuring great bridges, streams, and rivers.
Got lost a bit once I finished half the trail and ended up in a graveyard, but it was very nice overall and would recommend!

The trail is beautiful. I really do wish dog owners would just respect that it is not an off-leash park/trail. I nearly got attacked by a dog because the owner didn’t leash him when we crossed each other on the trail - growled, barked and charged towards me.
Please, if you are a dog owner, leash your dog when approaching other people - you don’t know how traumatizing an encounter with a dog can be. It’s just the right thing to do. No need to make comments like oh it’s just a puppy, oh my dog is friendly - until they are not.

A moderate trail with good variety of greenery, streams, and hill climbs. There are very busy parts near evergreen brickworks with families, kids, lots of dogs off leash. Then it goes into a quieter and hilly area that’s quite nice. The last quarter of the trail was all road / sidewalk walking. It’s good for an urban walk for sure.
A straightforward trail. Easy and beautiful, but nothing extraordinary.
Muddy/mucky in spots but overall great

Nice urban hike. Conditions were fine. Some construction and closed sections. I seem to have lost the trail near the end and finished by walking neighborhood streets. 
The lil stop at Brickworks was nice. Bathrooms and a look around before continuing the loop

this trail involves leaving the path and walking in the neighbourhood. still a nice walk tho! on weekends during the summer, they have a market going on with food & vintage clothing + more. easy trail, well kept!
Good loop until the end where you just walk on the street/bridge
Closer to the end, beware of the inaccurate bridge crossing. The trail shows to go underneath it, but that's impossible. Must go up top
Good trail with nice view
A short portion of trail goes beside the busy road beside highway,  interesting.
Towards end of the trail, it’s  closed off due to construction
Really nice trail, parts of it were closed for maintenance but otherwise very nice walk.
Nice trail. Doesn’t even feel like you’re in the city. Many different routes to take, from paved to dirt trail. Definitely coming here again.
Great loop except the Balfour section is closed for construction. I took a detour that was pleasant for a plan b option.
Early spring, so a little muddy, but lovely long trail!
There’s some construction on parts of the path. Tricky if you don’t know where you’re going.
Some slippery ice

Parts of the trail was closed off, due to construction, however I found a way to go around it. 
Also I got diverted off the trail and had to figure out how to get back on. It was quite the adventure.
Snow made some parts of this hike really slippery. I’m thinking when summer comes around they will open up other parts of the trail.  It was great, definitely worth it.

A large section on the west side of the loop is closed due to construction from 4.2k to 5.3 on the main AllTrails map. In addition, the side trail is closed just north of the railroad tracks, where there are stairs to the street. The rest of the trail was in excellent condition & the snow was well packed.
Lots of cool bridges! Maybe a deer carcass but don’t worry about it! Icy!

You actually have to cross the bridge, make a left at the first Street and then follow it until you see a pathway leading back onto the trail.  At the bottom of the pathway it is blocked my construction that you have to navigate around.
Closed just south of St Claire. Visitors generally respect the dogs must be leashed signs, affluent locals ignore them. Still, a beautiful trail this time of year.

The trail starts off leading you through what seems to be a scenic forest terrain, but then takes you on a 2 km hike along the streets, leading you off the beaten path only to make a quick U-turn right back onto the same street, which makes no sense. Eventually, you are led back into the trail area, only to find it blocked off, making it impossible to complete the journey. We had to turn around and walk the 4 km back the way we came. Please note, the trail is under construction until February 2025.
Some paths of the main trail for  little more challenge
Nice park in the middle of the city. Great for fall hikes.

It is a beautiful trail. I got lost at one point and ended up at Yonge street. I had to walk 3 kilometres to get to my car haha. Finally found out that part of the trail is closed due to construction.

Lots of bikes on the way. If you go on a Saturday, I’d recommend stopping by the brick works market. Overall, pretty good trail.
Last staircase was blocked off - had to cut through cemetery

staircase at the end is blocked off, so we had to cut through a cemetery. Spooky vibes, but perfect for this spooky October season. Heath Crescent staircase still closed. If you're not willing to hop the barrier, cut through Mount Pleasant Cemetery
High bike traffic but nice trail
Until you get to don valley quarry/garden area the trail has quite a bit of garbage and doesn’t seem well taken care of. After that point though it’s well maintained.

Beautiful! Fun and easy hike.
Great trails, farmers market at the end was a nice surprise

Nice walk for the afternoon. A bit of mud and puddles after the rain yesterday but they were all navigable even with regular footwear. The stairs to Heath Cr. were closed so we detoured through Mt. Pleasant cemetery.
Great trail. A lot of dogs off the the leash.
Nice and shady trail for hiking. Recommend!

Hilly but very cool on a hot summer day.

Amazing exposure to several bridges, mg favourite. Trail was paved/pea gravel or dirt in some locations. Easy run/wall. Trail head closed at steep stairs. Residential walk around, not ideal. Trail very messy with brush/ some muddy parts.

Very nice loop in the ravine. Quite peaceful excepts for the few parts near the highway.

Great hike! Loved wandering through the Brickworks around the halfway point. There were lots of mucky and icy spots. Two sections were blocked off. One on the northside of St.Clair as you descend again into the ravine travelling north around the 3/4 mark of loop. Do not try it in snowy or icy weather. The other shortly afterward as you head east back up the STEEP blocked off stairs ascending out of the ravine to the charming little neighborhood just west of Mt. Pleasant Rd. The barrier at the top is easily moved after releasing the loop of chains at left. Do not try it in snowy or icy weather either.
Lots of muddy spots. Some icy patches. Overall walkable thought
Lots of ice on the trails
A lot of dogs! Only way to make a loop is to use sidewalks for last quarter or so. Crampons a good idea. Stop at brickworks for washrooms and hot drinks.

During the winter it can be very icy.
You can stop at brickworks for a coffee.
You can park in the cemetery at the funeral chapel.
Sometimes you hear urban noises be mindful if you’re looking for a pure nature

This is a super loop trail in heart of the city.  Great all year round. Can easily be extended by looping in Mt. Pleasant cemetery or going into the Brickworks trail section.   Need traction aids in winter.
Great trail bit part of it has been closed due to erosion. Not sure how to make up the loop now without illegally going through the closed and blocked off section at the end
glorious on a warm November day. meandered through scenic rivers and through the market at evergreen Brickworks
Quite a nice loop trail. Stopped at the Brickworks farmers market halfway through.

In early September, it's a lovely afternoon walk

Nice but most people walk their dogs off leash  and some motorized bikes and scooters going pretty fast
Fabulous city trail. One of the best in 416!!  Two ravines loop and side loop in Brickworks. Great all hear round.  Moore Park ravine trailhead still affected by construction.
Great trail. Few constructions to be aware

BEWARE - Lots of closures. The beginning of the trail is closed for construction, and the second entrance is also closed due to the steps. We found a way in but had to take a big detour and it’s tough to find your way back around if it’s your first time. We decided to walk to the brickworks and are catching an Uber Back to the car.

It's a nice walk and a much better way for me to walk downtown without using many city streets. Unfortunately, it's been under partial reconstruction for years. These days a major section, heading south from Moore Avenue, is populated by heavy equipment churning up the landscape. Boo! to Parks and Recreation, who seem to have no interest in getting the job finished in a timely manner.

This trail is currently under heavy construction almost all the way down to the Brickworks, so unless you like maneuvering over rocks and bricks with caution tape fencing both sides, it might be worth waiting until the work is done. Otherwise it looks like it will be a lovely path!
I think it might be better in spring or fall, a lot of the path was so icy and I nearly wiped out several times. Parts were way busier than others.
Too busy.
Very muddy and still rather city-esque. With it being winter, ita probably because of the lack of leaves. Might be worth driving another 10 minutes out of the city to for a bit more ambiance.
Super icy and part was blocked off. Otherwise a nice hike.
Awesome trail through woods! Wide snowy trail- so beautiful

It’s not a loop. I started from the trailhead at Avoca Ave./ David Balfour Park trail, through Evergreen brickwork, then on to belt line trail , to Moore Ravine park, there is construction from Heath St., so have to finish there.

This was a good walk with some elevation (mostly light climbs and stairs), lots of creek and shady trails. A short detour through the brickworks gave us the opportunity to see a big snapping turtle in the marshes. 

We intended to go up to Moore on the beltline and through the Mt. Pleasant cemetery before heading back to where we parked on Heath West but a trail closure meant we had to exit the trail at Heath East and walk through the neighbourhood before dipping in to the ravine and back up.

The trail was okay. But the route to the exit was confusing and we were stuck at the Mt. Pleasant Cemetery for more than 30 min because the door was locked. We tried to call Uber but they can't get in either. So we started walking to the gate by Mt. Pleasant Street. That's when we saw the security guard and he opened the gate for us. The worest part -  the Cemetery has an awful lighting - sorry absolutely no lighting. It was very dark and you could put yourself into one of the horror movies just by staying for few minutes.
Good trail, stairs closed by the cemetery
Half of the loop is close to the highway, very disturbing

The loop was fun. You walk through forest, shaded areas, a cemetery, and there's lots of options to go on little detours. I found the path a little hard to follow and I had to cross some busy roads. The trail isn't clearly marked so I needed my phone/map a lot and I spent an extra hour lost in the cemetery. I parked at the Brickworks and the cost was $8 for 3+ hours.

I love this city walk. Beautiful and mainly tree canopied. Not particularly busy, compared to the Kay Gardner Beltline Trail. A stroller is doable but wouldn’t be easy on a couple of the hills and stones, which aren’t plentiful but still occasionally unavoidable. Be sure to enter the Brickworks while on the walk—prepare to be wowed. Watch out for bikers who seem reticent to ring their bells. And the omnipresent pet owners who refuse to follow City Bylaws and leash their dogs. The trail near St Clair and Yonge can be deserted and a little scary for a woman who is alone.
Great trail in the city. Kids love the flowers and ponds.
snowy and a bit icy, boots for sure
amazing very beautiful
love very beautiful

IT WAS ONE OF THE MOST BEAUTIFUL TRAILS IVE GONE TO. A real hidden gem I will bring my mom and friends here next time. Sooo much shade and tall old trees which is not as common on trails that I’ve gone in lately. Very well taken care of with not a piece of litter in SITE! 20/10 must see trail if your visiting the city :)

Beautiful trail with a good combo of overpasses and nature! Lots of kids and dogs out enjoying the different spots alongside Mud Creek. Definitely some stretches that were too icy to enjoy but you can always detour into Mt Pleasant Cemetery or Evergreen Brick Works!
it was pretty busy for the first couple kms, but a stretch in the last third was empty but very narrow and slippery next to a 10ft drop. be careful!

One of the best trails in Toronto, simply due to the views and feeling like you’re out of the city. Do it early or it’s hard to socially distance. Stunning in the fall.

Great. Relaxing. Helps to be with yourself. Though many parts are along busy roads so not completely wild.
Most of the trail is fairly wide which is nice. It’s nowhere nearly as busy as the the Beltline trail but it is fairly isolated at dusk/dawn so plan your trip accordingly.

Lots of dogs walking, some off leash but very friendly. People were all pleasant to talk to along the trail. Shaded & sunny areas. Mostly gravel trails with some paved.

Great trail! Family/dog friendly. Lots of beautiful scenery. There are ponds that have turtles and frogs in them, very cute! Lots of shade as well when walking through the belt line path. Highly recommend!
Feel like you are away from the city.  There were beautiful tall trees along with trail and pretty easy and short walk. It leads to brick works which is a hidden tourist spot in toronto.
Fun running trail - gravel, dirt, pavement. Nicely shaded, wide paths with enough room for all the walkers, runners and cyclists. Challenging hills with wooden stairs.

Great trail to feel in touch with nature, see some cool bridges and artwork, just enough inclines to break a nice sweat without having to take a break, not overly busy on a Friday afternoon in August. I look forward to completing the whole loop on my next visit
Great place to have a nice hike with tonnes of shaded areas. Some parts are pretty bumpy with loose gravel but tonnes of people around so if you hurt yourself someone will see you :)
Nice trail. Didn’t know what to expect. Main trails all Gravelled. Some parts very bumpy. Better for jogging/hiking not biking. Lots of side trails. Will go again to explore those side trails
Good for hiking. Bike not so much!

I enjoyed it, , saw lots of people jogging and families  walking dogs, lots of trees provided shade while we walk. There was a moss, ponds with lilly pads, nice ravine, went up and down some steep hills. When you get to the top can see the CN Tower and buildings nice view.
Construction, too many people
Great city trail.  Nice to be in the woods in the City.  Heavily trafficked and some cyclists.
It is scenic and an easy hiking trail, so I agree with some of the reviews that it's better for hiking than biking due to the terrain and heavy foot traffic.

Parts of this trail are excellent but the map should be amended - due to construction and COVID, several areas are closed and require trail amendments.    When you’re not doing residential streets, It’s a beautiful, heavily shaded trail with wide paths and heavy foot traffic. Best part by far is the David Balfour Park ravine when you head into the smaller side trails.
Good local trail - easy, lots of traffic.

The trail is well-kept and fairly well-marked/straightforward, especially if you’re following along on the app. Relatively big chunks of it are closed off due to construction though, so you have to adjust your entrance and exit points. For the most part, the trail is really accessible for all hiking abilities and it’s nicely paved - plus you follow the river for quite a while which is peaceful. Can get muddy in the rain, beware! Again, sometimes due to closures you have to cut through more residential areas to continue sections of the hike, but all in all it’s a great lush route to make you feel as if you’ve really stepped away from the metropolis.

A beautiful trail tucked away in the city.  North area was blocked off due to construction and the cemetery hours (closed until 5-5:30 during the weekday) so we had to figure out how to get back on the trail via streets to complete the loop. 

Lots of shade and trees, with the sound of running water, and not too busy during the weekday- a great trail for walking and biking!
It’s a nice trail with some bridges and mud creek flows along there. There are dogs and most are not on leashes !!!
A nice forested detour on a wide trail that leaves from the main brickworks area. The best part is the "cave of dreams" - a mysterious and spooky tree in the heart of the woods. Lots of dog walkers.
Couple sketchy road crossings but overall great good
Trails like this one are a gem, amazing way to zone out while you're in middle of a city.

Excellent trail! It is quickly accessible from downtown, but will make you think you are far from the city! We followed the trail from start to (almost) finish. It is stroller- friendly despite a few bumps and muddy parts. The shadow and freshness provided by the trees in almost all the trail was greatly appreciated in this hot July day. The pause at Evergreen brickworks was the cherry on top of it all :-)

It’s pretty decent place to go hiking, but road in the app a bit wrong. We lost our way and didn’t finish it, because a ledder in the end was closed (private property). Anyway, overall the walk was good.

No trail markers so I would use this app while here to make sure you don’t end up on a side trail. Other than that the trail was clear. Had to take a round about way through a cemetery as when we got to the staircase back to the trail after cutting through the neighborhood it was blocked off for construction. Not sure how long that will last but the cemetery connects to the trail if you can’t get through. Get ready to run across a busy street though. Went on a weekday and it was fairly well trafficked so I can imagine it’s crowded on the weekends. Where I entered the trail there was a community center and cafe that look like a great place to bring kids. Overall a great area and trail!

Nice trail condition. Walkable I’m running shoes, no boots required. There is a staircase that is closed near the beginning, had to scramble around it a little bit, but otherwise the trail condition is great. You forget you are in Toronto for a while.
great trail. free street parking at the starting point.  take a break at the cafe belong at the other end.
Lovely trail in the city, that feels like you in the woods. one down side is part of the trail it blocked and your forced to take a different path.
Steps closed at Heath crt

One of the most beautiful trails in the midtown Toronto. You'll love running/hiking in the woods right next to Yellow creek and Mud creek. Grab a cup of coffee and a blueberry scone at Cafe Belong at Evergreen Brick Works - the lowest altitude in this loop. The wide and paved trails make it perfect for a rainy day. I've been doing this trail for 5 years now and never got tired of it.
A tough walk with much of the route iced up. Ok with crampons, a bit dodgy without as at mid- Mar 19!

Amazing hike in the city!
Very icy in the winter so wear good boots and go very slowly.
Street parking was available & close by.

This is a great trail in the middle of the city ! Looking forward to doing the whole loop in the summer - it’s currently a skating rink and slush in a lot of parts (as of March 10/19) and crampons for your shoes would be really helpful. Very difficult in some parts with the ice for what should be a very easy trail!
We walked with a stroller and it was great - paved road, forest feel
Beautiful trail in the heart of the city.  Family friendly with lots to do in and around the area.

Beautiful trail with many access points from the Evergreen Brickworks to Mount Pleasant Road, Moore Park, etc.  It's quiet throughout the week and moderate to heavy trafficed on the weekend.  It's also 1 mile longer than the original Moore Park trail Loop.

Mostly flat trails. We took the Moore Ave. trailhead entrance w/c is a bit hidden. Parking is just along the street, in front of the cemetery or one of the residential roads. It's nice that it connects to the Evergreen Brickworks. This will be a nice way to go on the Saturday Farmer's market in the morning when parking is packed :)

Very nice trail. Medium difficulty, paved and easy to follow. It goes cloes to an abandoned railway and offers great view over the city. I ended up in an old factory and clay quarry. A must do to my opinion.
Main entrances in second part closed you can’t follow the path as directed
This is a great trail Highly recommended
Trail partially closed at south east corner. Can get through fencing but only on weekends when workers are gone.

This was a pretty good trail, keep in mind this is in winter with feet of snow on the ground, cross-country skiiers were out there. Great for all types, easy trail, well owen in paths and the loop that goes through moore park to the brickworks is a great workout at about 7km.
Fun and adventurous trail!

Pretty busy trail, was under construction when we were there. But definitely beautiful and in a great location!
Not everyone has their dogs leashes, so be cautious of that if trekking with a pooch!

Absolutely loved this trail. 
The trail head at Moore Ave is kind of hidden and not signed at all. It's on the south side of the street.  Look for the "Mount Pleasant Visitation Centre" sign on the north side of the street as a landmark; trailhead is directly across from there. 
This is a great trail! Beautiful wooded area with rivers/creeks and tons of stuff to see and explore with kids. We went with a group of 8 adults and 8 kids (ages 2.5 - 7 yrs old) and this trail was perfect length and difficulty. Bonus is that we went on Sunday so at the exact halfway point, the brickworks farmer's market was happening so you can get delicious food. We stayed there for a while and then just hiked the same trail back. We didn't technically do the "loop" in that sense. 
Will do it again!!!!
Oh - I haven't mastered using this app to find my way in trails so i just asked ppl if I was going the right way towards the brickworks.
Nice easy graded loop. The stairway out of the ravine at the end is barred off, I had to wind my way out via going off-road in the cemetery instead.

This is a beautiful well-forested trail that almost makes you forget you are in the city, if it weren't for the sound of traffic.  It must be a great location to escape the heat in the summer.  If it wasn't for this app, I would have lost the loop.  There are many side trails leading off into likely the surrounding neighbourhoods.
Decent waking, Brickworks was the highlight of the trail.
Not very picturesque, but Brickworks is always nice
Very nice short trail from Moore Ave to the Brickworks.  Gorgeous colour in the fall.
Like this place for walking. Its one the best destination in Toronto.
